title: Place Value & Powers of 10
standard_text: Use place value understanding to solve real-life, mathematical problems (including relationships between places and powers of 10).

misconceptions.description: Student adds zeros as a separate number instead of shifting place value by factor of 10.
Student shifts decimal point in the wrong direction when multiplying or dividing by powers of 10.
Student adds 10 rather than multiplying by 10 when determining value of neighboring digits.

title: Decimal Addition and Subtraction
standard_text: Read, write, and compare decimal numbers to the thousandths place, and round and perform operations with decimal numbers to the hundredths place.

misconceptions.description: Student aligns decimal numbers to the right like whole numbers instead of lining up the decimal points.
Student fails to place a placeholder zero when subtracting from a shorter decimal.
Student treats the decimal point as a wall that resets regrouping.

title: Comparing & Rounding Decimals
standard_text: Read, write, and compare decimal numbers to the thousandths place, and round and perform operations with decimal numbers to the hundredths place.

misconceptions.description: Student assumes 0.125 is greater than 0.5 because 125 is greater than 5.
Student truncates digits instead of examining the deciding digit to round.
Student compares hundredths place directly to tenths place.

title: Adding & Subtracting Fractions
standard_text: Model and solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions and mixed numbers with unlike denominators.

misconceptions.description: Student adds numerators together and denominators together directly (e.g. 1/2 + 1/3 = 2/5).
Student changes denominators to common denominator but leaves original numerators unchanged.
In mixed number subtraction, student subtracts smaller fractional part from larger without borrowing.

title: Multiplying Fractions & Whole Numbers
standard_text: Model and solve problems involving multiplication of a fraction and a whole number.

misconceptions.description: Student multiplies both numerator and denominator by the whole number factor.
Student cannot conceptualize that multiplying by a fraction less than one scales down the product.
Student applies proportional cross-multiplication instead of multiplying numerators.

title: Division of Unit Fractions & Whole Numbers
standard_text: Model and solve problems involving division of a unit fraction by a whole number and a whole number by a unit fraction.

misconceptions.description: Student calculates whole / unit instead of unit / whole (e.g. 4 / (1/2) vs (1/2) / 4).
Student does not invert or realize how many unit parts partition the whole.
Student treats the resulting unit fraction as a remainder quantity.

title: Volume of Rectangular Prisms
standard_text: Investigate volume of right rectangular prisms by packing them with unit cubes without gaps or overlaps. Then, determine the total volume to solve problems.

misconceptions.description: Student counts visible outer faces instead of internal packed unit cubes.
Student calculates l + w + h instead of multiplying length × width × height.
Student calculates area of base (l × w) but neglects multiplying by number of layers.

title: Multi-Digit Multiplication
standard_text: Multiply and divide multi-digit whole numbers to solve relevant, mathematical problems.

misconceptions.description: Student neglects placing zero placeholder when multiplying by tens or hundreds digit.
Student multiplies carried numbers instead of adding them after multiplying digits.
Student shifts partial products unevenly across column places.

title: Multi-Digit Division with Remainders
standard_text: Multiply and divide multi-digit whole numbers to solve relevant, mathematical problems.

misconceptions.description: Student treats remainder as simple decimal or forgets to interpret rounding up in contextual word problems.
Student miscalculates intermediate subtraction during standard long division algorithm.
Student writes first quotient digit over wrong place value.

title: Order of Operations & Expressions
standard_text: Write, interpret, and evaluate numerical expressions within authentic problems.

misconceptions.description: Student evaluates operations strictly left-to-right without prioritizing multiplication/division before addition.
Student always performs addition before subtraction instead of evaluating left-to-right.
Student skips inner grouped terms inside parentheses.

title: Ratios & Equivalent Ratios
standard_text: Explain the concept of a ratio, represent ratios, and use ratio language to describe a relationship between two quantities.

misconceptions.description: Student adds a constant number to both parts of ratio instead of scaling by multiplication (e.g. 2:3 becomes 3:4 instead of 4:6).
Student confuses part-to-part ratio (cats to dogs) with part-to-whole ratio (cats to total pets).
Student writes ratio terms in reversed order from the question context.

title: Unit Rates & Unit Pricing
standard_text: Describe the concept of rates and unit rate in the context of a ratio relationship.

misconceptions.description: Student calculates quantity / cost instead of cost / quantity to find unit price.
Student leaves rate unsimplified with non-unit denominator.
Student confuses distance-per-hour with hours-per-distance.

title: Percents as Rates per 100
standard_text: Calculate a percent of a quantity as a rate per 100 and solve everyday problems given a percent.

misconceptions.description: Student converts 5% to 0.5 instead of 0.05.
Student multiplies value directly by 25 instead of 0.25 when finding 25% of a number.
Student finds the discounted amount instead of final remaining cost.

title: Dividing Fractions by Fractions
standard_text: Multiply and divide any combination of whole numbers, fractions, and mixed numbers using a student-selected strategy, and interpret products/quotients.

misconceptions.description: Student inverts first fraction instead of second fraction (the divisor).
Student divides numerator by numerator and denominator by denominator without common denominators.
Student inverts both fractions prior to multiplication.

title: Multi-Digit Decimal Operations
standard_text: Perform operations with multi-digit decimal numbers fluently using models and strategies.

misconceptions.description: Student places decimal point in multiplication product based on whole number digits.
In division, student forgets to shift dividend decimal point when shifting divisor.
Student writes 0.6 instead of 0.06 when product has two decimal digits.

title: Integers & Opposites on Number Lines
standard_text: Identify and compare integers and explain the meaning of zero based on multiple authentic situations.

misconceptions.description: Student believes -8 is greater than -3 because 8 is greater than 3.
Student thinks absolute value of -5 is -5 or changes sign regardless of context.
Student orders negatives left-to-right as -1, -2, -3 starting from negative infinity.

title: Generating Equivalent Expressions
standard_text: Apply the properties of operations to identify and generate equivalent expressions.

misconceptions.description: Student multiplies outer coefficient by first term only (e.g. 3(x + 4) = 3x + 4).
Student adds variable and constant terms together (e.g. 4x + 5 = 9x).
Student forgets that distributing a negative changes the signs of all inside terms.

title: Solving One-Step Equations
standard_text: Write and solve one-step equations and inequalities as mathematical models to explain authentic, realistic situations.

misconceptions.description: Student adds when the equation has addition instead of subtracting (e.g. x + 5 = 12 -> x = 17).
Student performs the inverse operation on one side without balancing the equal sign.
In 3x = 15, student multiplies 15 by 3 instead of dividing by 3.

title: Measures of Center: Mean & Median
standard_text: Describe and interpret the center of the distribution by the equal share value (mean).

misconceptions.description: Student selects middle number from an unsorted data list.
Student divides total sum by 2 instead of total count of data values.
Student averages middle numbers when asked for sum / count.

title: Numerical Expressions with Exponents
standard_text: Write and evaluate numerical expressions involving rational bases and whole-number exponents.

misconceptions.description: Student calculates base × exponent instead of repeated multiplication (e.g. 2^3 = 6 instead of 8).
Student believes any non-zero base to power 0 equals 0 instead of 1.
Student evaluates 3^2 as 2^3.
